text:
tess: Heads-up — trying the terraform + docker quickstart (local infra) and first call fails with 403. Using a service account JSON mounted into the container and REDWOOD_API_KEY env set. App logs show 'service token missing' then refresh 403. Anyone seen this with mounted creds?

devex-bot: Filed DEVEX-5231. Please paste minimal logs and env details.

harry: Mounting service account json into container is fine, but the quickstart expects a workspace-capable key or the CLI dev token. If your org hasn't accepted billing/terms the refresh path is blocked.

tess: Snippet:

```
docker-compose up --build
[2026-03-10T09:12:01Z] INFO auth: lookup service token
[2026-03-10T09:12:01Z] ERROR auth: refresh failed 403 Forbidden
Error: refresh auth failed: 403
    at refreshAuth (/app/node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/auth.js:120:19)
```

nina: Quick checks: 1) Is the service account key a workspace-scoped key (created by org admin)? Those can be subject to org gating. 2) Try running `npx @redwood/cli login` locally (not in container) to generate ~/.redwood/token and bind-mount it into the container as a quick dev workaround.

tess: CLI login worked when I mounted ~/.redwood/token into the container. App now returns 200.

harry: Follow-up: we'll update the quickstart README to call out org billing gating when using service/workspace keys, and add better SDK errors that suggest "try personal API key or CLI login" when refresh returns 403 and no cached token.

nina: Filed a small DX task to add that hint and an example docker-compose bind mount. Also proposing a new SDK error code `ERR_FIRSTCALL_BILLING` to make programmatic detection easier.

tess: Thanks, saves a lot of debugging time :pray:
